Information Security Management System (ISMS) Policy Summaries
A Consolidated Overview of Key ISMS Policies
04-06-2026
Building Trust, Quality & Growth Together

- Kreate Technologies

Purpose:Ensure only authorized users access information systems, based on least privilege and need-to-know principles.
Scope:Applies to all system administrators, servers, VMs, network equipment, applications, and infrastructure.
Key Highlights:
User Access: Unique IDs, no shared accounts, formal access requests, periodic reviews.
Privileged Access: Strictly controlled, requires joint authorization, subject to MFA and logging.
Network Access: No unauthorized hardware/software, VPNs must be secure, no dual network connections.
Internet Access: Restricted by role, monitored usage, blocked categories (e.g., social media, gambling).
Wireless Access: Authenticated access only, guest access limited to filtered internet.
Required Records/Evidence
User Access Records
Unique user IDs and access levels.
Group ID approvals and periodic reviews.
Privileged access approvals and logs (e.g., root, domain admin).
Access revocation logs (especially for exiting employees).
Access Review Documentation
Periodic access reviews (at least twice a year).
Justifications and approvals for access requests.
Exit Management Records
HR requests for user/email ID removal.
Device and data clearance checklists.
Data backup records for exiting employees.
Network Access Logs
IP address assignments.
VPN access approvals and logs.
Antivirus scan reports for external systems.
Internet Access Records
Internet access approvals.
Website access requests and approvals.
Logs of blocked categories and exceptions.
Wireless Access Logs
Guest access logs.
Collaboration tool usage records.

🔐 1. Access Management Policy

Purpose:Protect IT systems and data from malware, viruses, and other malicious threats.
Scope:Applies to all company-owned and BYOD devices connected to the organization’s network.
Key Highlights:
Mandatory AV Software: All Windows systems must have company-standard antivirus installed.
Updates & Scans: Daily DAT updates, thrice-weekly scans, weekly scheduled scans.
Infected Devices: Must be isolated until verified clean.
Removable Media: Must be scanned before use.
Exceptions: Allowed only with documented protection plans.
Awareness: Users must avoid suspicious files/emails and report incidents immediately.
Required Records/Evidence
Antivirus Installation and Update Logs
Installation records on all Windows systems.
Daily DAT update logs from antivirus server.
Scanning Reports
Endpoint scan logs (thrice weekly).
Weekly scheduled scan logs for all assets.
Incident Reports
Reports of virus/worm activity.
Actions taken (e.g., isolation, cleaning).
Exception Documentation
Justifications for systems without antivirus.
Plans for protection of such systems.
Review Records
Bi-annual internal review of infrastructure.
List of assets not updated for more than 15 days.
Removable Media Scan Logs
USB/Hard Drive scan reports before use.
🛡️ 2. Anti-Virus Policy

Purpose:Ensure critical business data is regularly backed up, securely stored, and restorable in case of loss or disaster.
Scope:Covers all systems, applications, databases, and files storing critical or confidential data.
Key Highlights:
Employee Responsibilities: Store data in OneDrive, avoid unproductive software.
IT Responsibilities: Daily/weekly/monthly backups, retention policies, use of Acronis, secure storage (NAS, Cloud, Tape).
Backup Procedures: Scheduled backups with user notifications, encrypted off-site storage.
Restoration Checks: Quarterly tests with documentation.
Reporting: Automated logs, issue tracking, and governance by IT Manager.
Required Records/Evidence
Backup Logs
Daily/weekly/monthly backup logs.
Backup type, source/destination, status, volume, errors.
Restoration Test Records
Restoration test dates, systems/data restored, outcomes, issues.
Backup Infrastructure Documentation
Backup media and location records (NAS, Cloud, Tape).
Tape movement logs and encryption status.
Reporting and Governance
Backup trackers (success/failure, root cause, resolution).
IT Manager and engineer communication logs.
Retention and Storage Records
Retention periods (e.g., 30-day OneDrive, 7-day attendance DB).
Physical security checks for tape storage.
Policy Enforcement Logs
Deletion of unproductive/unauthorized content.
Compliance checks for data hygiene.

Scope:Applies to all employees and vendors responsible for equipment maintenance.
Key Highlights:
Security Controls: UPS for all PCs, environmental monitoring, insurance, and maintenance logs.
Media Handling: Secure disposal of storage devices; no off-site movement without authorization.
Cabling: Secure installation, labeling, and maintenance; separation of power and data lines.

Purpose:Define rules for employees using personal devices to access company systems, ensuring data security and compliance.
Scope:Applies to all employees, contractors, and third parties using personal devices for work.

Device Eligibility: Only approved, secure devices allowed.
Security Requirements: Antivirus, encryption, remote wipe, no jailbreaking.
Access Control: MFA and role-based access required.

Exit Procedure: Company data must be removed from personal devices upon termination.
Enforcement: Violations may lead to disciplinary action or termination.

Asset Types: Includes hardware, software, information, paper, and intellectual property.

Scope:Applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party vendors at Kreate Technologies.

Usage Restrictions: Only HODs may use removable media with proper approval.
Approval Process: USB access must be time-bound and approved by HOD and Infra Head.

Scope:Applies to all employees using organizational email systems.
Key Highlights:
Professional Use: Emails must be used for business purposes only.
Security: Avoid sending sensitive data without authorization; antivirus must be active.
Restrictions: No spoofing, chain mails, or inappropriate content; no executable attachments.
Monitoring: Emails may be monitored with senior management approval.
Compliance: Regular audits; violations may lead to disciplinary action.

Scope:Applies to all employees, contractors, and third parties accessing organizational data.
Key Highlights:
Cryptography Controls: Mobile devices must not store official data; backups required; software installation controlled by IT.

🔐 11. Encryption and Cryptography Control Policy

Purpose:Ensure secure separation of development, testing, staging, and production environments to prevent unauthorized access or changes.
Scope:Applies to all users managing or accessing code and environments.
Key Highlights:
Development: Access for TL/PM and developers; no access for QA.
Testing (QA): Access for TL/PM and QA (read-only); no access for developers.
Staging/UAT: Access for TL/PM; customers get read-only access.
Production: Only PM/Infra Manager and Release Manager have written access.
Promotion Requirements: Each phase requires defect logging, code reviews, and approvals before moving to the next.
Required Records/Evidence
Access Control Logs
Role-based access records for each environment (Dev, QA, UAT, Prod).
Code Review and Testing Records
Code review completion, defect logs in Jira, unit testing reports.

Build labelling, release notes, deployment instructions.

🧪 12. Environment Segregation Policy

Purpose:Define a consistent framework for classifying, labeling, handling, and destroying information assets based on sensitivity and business impact.
Scope:Applies to all employees, contractors, third parties, and all information assets across all formats and environments.
Key Highlights:
Classification Levels:
Business Confidential – Contractual/Legal
Business Confidential
Internal (default)
Unclassified
Responsibilities: Asset owners must classify and label information; reclassification allowed by superiors or based on time/events.
Labeling: Clear labeling required for each classification; encryption and IRM tools recommended.
Handling: Access on a need-to-know basis; secure storage and destruction required.
Unauthorized Acts: Strict penalties for unauthorized access, sharing, or tampering.
Destruction: Must follow the defined destruction policy with proper records.
Required Records/Evidence
Classification Records
Initial classification by asset owner or creator.
Reclassification logs (event/time-based or superior-directed).
Labeling Documentation
Labeling of documents/media with classification tags (e.g., BC-C/L, Business Confidential).
Use of IRM tools or encryption for classified documents.
Access Logs
Logs of access to Business Confidential – Contractual/Legal information.
Audit trails for classified information.
Storage and Handling Records
Secure storage location documentation.
Marking of physical folders/files.
Destruction Records
Logs of destruction of classified information per Destruction Policy.
Audit Certificates
Internal audit team certificates for classified information verification.
🗂️ 13. Information Security Classification Policy

Purpose:Ensure protection and responsible handling of PII in compliance with laws and organizational standards.
Scope:Applies to all personnel and systems handling PII within the organization.
Key Highlights:
PII Includes: Names, DOB, IDs (PAN, Aadhaar), contact info, financial and health data, biometrics.
Policy Requirements:
Classify PII as confidential.
Restrict access using role-based controls.
Encrypt PII in transit and at rest.
Use secure channels for transmission.
Store in access-controlled environments.
Retain only as long as necessary; securely dispose.
Incident Response: Breaches must be reported and handled per the incident management policy.
Compliance: Non-compliance may lead to disciplinary or legal action.
Required Records/Evidence
PII Classification Records
Labelling and classification of PII as Confidential.
Access Control Logs
Role-based access records.
Access reviews and authentication logs.
Encryption Logs
Encryption status for PII in transit and at rest.
Encryption in software solutions.
Transmission Records
Secure channel usage logs.
Avoidance of unencrypted transmission.
Storage Records
Secure storage location documentation.
Access permission reviews.
Retention and Disposal Logs

Secure disposal records (shredding, deletion).

Breach reports and resolution documentation.
Reference to Incident Management Process.
Compliance Documentation
Legal and regulatory compliance records (e.g., IT Act, GDPR).

Report unusual behavior, malware, or data loss.
Disconnect infected systems and avoid using removable media.

Purpose:Establish guidelines for using web filtering technology to ensure a secure and productive online environment.
Scope:Applies to all employees, devices, remote users, and third parties accessing the company’s internet or systems.
Key Highlights:
Filtering System: Blocks access to risky or non-work-related websites via firewall and antivirus.
Blocked Categories: Adult content, gambling, hacking, malware, phishing, and social media (unless work-related).
Monitoring: Web activity is monitored; logs and reports may be reviewed.
Exceptions: Can be requested through IT for legitimate business needs.
Enforcement: Violations may lead to disciplinary or legal action.

🔄 17. Change Management Policy

Purpose:Ensure all software developed or maintained follows secure coding practices to protect data and systems.
Scope:Applies to in-house, third-party, and open-source development.
Key Highlights:
Coding Standards: Follow OWASP and language-specific guidelines.
Input Validation: Prevent vulnerabilities like SQL injection and XSS.
Authentication & Authorization: Use strong mechanisms and least privilege.
Encryption: Required for data in transit and at rest.
Error Handling: Avoid exposing system details.
Logging & Monitoring: Capture and review security-relevant events.
Secure SDLC: Integrate security into all development phases.
Code Reviews: Mandatory using tools like SonarQube.
Third-Party Components: Must be vetted and monitored (e.g., via Snyk).
Training: Ongoing developer education on secure practices.
Compliance: Align with OWASP, PCI DSS, and legal standards.

Implementation records for input sanitization.

Surveillance: CCTV monitoring with footage retained for at least 30 days.

🏢 19. Physical Security Policy

Purpose:Prevent unauthorized access to sensitive information by ensuring workspaces and screens are kept clear.
Scope:Applies to all employees, workspaces (on-site, remote, hybrid), and devices used for business.
Key Highlights:
Desk Management: Lock away confidential documents and avoid leaving sensitive items on desks.
Screen Security: Use screen savers with auto-lock after 5 minutes; avoid desktop shortcuts to sensitive files.
Document Handling: Shred confidential waste; remove prints immediately from printers.
Meeting Rooms: Clear whiteboards, clipboards, and notes post-meeting.
Awareness: Security teams may leave “Something Missing” notices to reinforce compliance.

parent_16.text:
💻 21. ICT Readiness for Business Continuity Policy

Purpose:Ensure secure and authorized transfer of information across all mediums to protect confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
Scope:Applies to all forms of information transfer—cloud-based, physical, verbal, and electronic.
Key Highlights:
Authorization: Transfers must be approved by the information owner.
Responsibility: The sender must assess risks and ensure proper authorization.
Methods: Use secure channels (e.g., encrypted email, approved cloud platforms); avoid SMS or unauthorized mobile apps.
Bulk Transfers: Require department head approval and logging by IT.
Fax & Physical Transfers: Must follow strict verification and confidentiality protocols.
Exceptions: Can be granted by CISO, IT Manager, or Technical Support Supervisor.
Required Records/Evidence
Transfer Authorization Logs
Approvals from Information Owners (e.g., CC in emails).
Head of Department approvals for bulk transfers.
Transfer Method Documentation
Records of chosen transfer media (email, fax, physical, cloud).
Risk assessments for each transfer.
Recipient Authentication Logs
Verification of recipient identity and authorization.
Transfer Logs
Maintained by IT for routine and ad-hoc bulk transfers (e.g., AD, applications).
Fax Transmission Records
Confirmation of correct number, transmission success, and secure disposal.

Scope:Applies to all outsourced development activities involving third-party vendors or freelancers.
Key Highlights:
Vendor Selection: Based on technical capability, security posture, and compliance (e.g., ISO 27001).
Contracts: Must include clauses for data protection, IP rights, incident reporting, and audit rights.
Access Control: Role-based access, MFA, and secure environments (e.g., VPN, isolated VMs).
Secure Development: Adherence to OWASP, code reviews, version control.
Monitoring: Regular oversight, access logs, and status reviews.
Testing: Includes security (VAPT), performance, and compliance validation.
Delivery & Post-Review: Secure code transfer, documentation, and vendor performance evaluation.

Vendor Evaluation Records

🧑‍💻 ISMS-PR-07: Outsourced Development Process
Purpose:Define secure use of personal devices for work while protecting organizational data and systems.
Scope:Applies to all employees, contractors, and affiliates using personal devices for work.
Key Highlights:
Approval & NDA: Formal request, IT inspection, and NDA signing required.
Device Requirements: Latest OS, antivirus, full-disk encryption, secure apps only.
Access Control: MFA, strong passwords, auto-lock after 5 minutes.
Data Handling: Encrypted storage and transmission; cloud-based storage preferred.
Monitoring: Devices must be registered with MDM; subject to audits.
Incident Response: Mandatory reporting; remote wipe enabled for lost/stolen devices.
Enforcement: Non-compliance may lead to access suspension or disciplinary action.

📱 ISMS-PR-08: Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) Process
Purpose:Standardize and control changes to applications and infrastructure to minimize disruption and risk.
Scope:Covers all application and infrastructure changes across production and non-production environments.
Key Highlights:
Change Types: Standard, Normal (Low/Medium/High Risk), Emergency, Informational.
Risk Assessment: Based on user impact, criticality, testability, and coordination.
Approval Workflow: Varies by risk level; includes CAB (Change Advisory Board) , TRB (Technical Review Board), and client approvals.
Roles:
Requester: Initiates change.
Owner: Manages implementation and communication.
Reviewers: Assess technical feasibility.
CAB: Approves high-risk changes.
KPIs: Track change volume, emergency change reduction, and fast-track usage.

DPDP-Act-2023 Children’s Data Protection Policy
Purpose: Safeguard children’s personal data and ensure compliance with DPDP Act 2023.
Scope: Applies to all data controllers/processors handling children’s personal data.
Key Highlights:
Consent: Obtain verifiable parental/guardian consent before processing.
Well-being: Processing must not harm the child’s safety or development.
Restrictions: No behavioral tracking or profiling of children.
Advertising: Prohibit targeted ads directed at children.

DPDP-Act-2023 Data Breach Response Policy
Purpose: Ensure timely detection, reporting, and mitigation of data breaches.
Scope: Covers all employees, contractors, and third-party processors with access to sensitive data.
Key Highlights:
Notification: Report to Data Protection Board and affected individuals within 72 hours.
Remediation: Apply immediate corrective actions.
Prohibitions: Concealment or delayed disclosure is strictly prohibited.
Impact Assessment: All breaches must undergo risk/impact evaluation.

DPDP-Act-2023 Consent Management Policy
Purpose: Ensure transparent and user-friendly handling of consent.
Scope: Applies to all employees, systems, and services collecting user consent.
Key Highlights:
Consent Managers: Use registered systems for consent collection and withdrawal.
Clarity: Present requests in clear, plain language.
Prohibitions: Do not bundle unrelated consents.
Withdrawal: Ensure users can easily withdraw consent.
